newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Horse racing-Star New Zealand stallion put down.
newsitem.headline: Horse racing-Star New Zealand stallion put down.

text.p: Sir Tristram, one of Australasia's greatest stallions, was buried on Thursday after being put down following a fall at New Zealand's Cambridge Stud.
Cambridge owner Patrick Hogan told national radio the 26-year-old horse, whose 620 progeny included 42 Group One winners, broke his leg on Wednesday, apparently while galloping in a paddock.
Hogan's stud is a compulsory stop for international bloodstock experts, including Britain's Queen Elizabeth, who have visited New Zealand.
Sir Tristram was Cambridge's leading sire, with progeny which included the big mare Empire Rose, winner of the 1987 Melbourne Cup, as well as more than 40 offspring now themselves at stud.
Industry experts described Sir Tristram, affectionately known as Paddy after his Irish roots, as the greatest of New Zealand's throughbred stallions.
The son of Sir Ivor was brought to New Zealand in 1976 aged five after Hogan paid NZ$160,000 for him and made him Cambridge's foundation sire.
Sir Tristram's service fee rose as high as NZ$220,000 during a stud career which ended with his retirement at the end of the last breeding season.
